bullets.title: SOX +81% in Q2 — record quarterly gain; semis on track for strongest H1 in decades
bullets.body: The SOX index rose 81% in Q2 2026, its best quarterly return since 1994, and is up ~93% YTD per Citi. The NDX gained ~25% in Q2, its best quarter since Q2 2020, while SMH is up ~75% YTD and 96% H1. Despite the record run, realized volatility in SMH hit 1-year highs at 72.1 — 19.3pts above 1M implied — as investors begin questioning valuations and bubble risk.

bullets.title: Mag 7 lost $2.3T in June — worst month in over a year, now down 3% YTD
bullets.body: Mag 7 stocks declined ~10% in June amid AI capex scrutiny, megacap rotation, and valuation concerns, representing a $2.3T drawdown. The group is now down 3% YTD despite the broader S&P 500 being up ~14% QTD (on track for best quarter since Q2 2020). JPM flags that HF semis positioning is at +3z zscore with mean-reversion risk, and tech hardware exposure is at >+4z — historically a peak signal.

bullets.title: Tightening financial conditions = risk to AI winners; MS recommends short semis/memory, long hyperscalers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley warns that if 2yr yields break above 4.2% (signaling core inflation >0.21% MoM), AI thematic winners face significant downside: the MS Broad AI index (+73% YTD) carries deeply negative beta to financial conditions, with the CPU basket (+165%) and Memory basket (+358%) showing intensifying sensitivity. The Price Momentum factor is at the 94th percentile of volatility, with top-decile names contributing 8.4pp of S&P's 8.8% YTD return. Recommended trade: buy MSFT Jan 410 calls, sell 2x 470 calls at near-zero cost.

bullets.title: Pension quarter-end rebalancing: ~$66-88B equity-to-bond shift overhanging the tape
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank estimates $88.3B in equities to sell and $44.4B in fixed income to buy by defined benefit pensions at quarter end. Goldman estimates $24B in US equity sales (92nd percentile since 2000). UBS separately notes pension rebalancing as a ~$66B equities-to-bonds headwind alongside record $170B ETF inflows in Q2.

bullets.title: NFP Thursday expected ~115-125K; Fed Chair Warsh speaks Wednesday — no policy guidance expected
bullets.body: JPM's Feroli forecasts 125K nonfarm payrolls vs. Street's 110K estimate, with the resilient labor market cited as an equity support. New Fed Chair Warsh speaks Wednesday at ECB Sintra but is not expected to provide policy color. 2yr yields are up ~1.4bps to 4.123%, 10yr up 1.6bps to 4.390%; the key threshold to watch is a 2yr break above 4.2%.

bullets.title: Memory prices inflecting hard: DRAM +20% QoQ in 3Q26 forecast; feeding ~30bps into core PCE
bullets.body: Mizuho supply chain checks forecast DRAM prices up 20% QoQ and NAND 20%+ QoQ in 3Q26, with DDR5 already up 20% since May and HBM pricing expectations rising for 2027. Goldman notes Korea's Samsung/SK Group plan to double DRAM capacity within 5 years (currently only ~50% of demand). Separately, higher memory prices have already added ~30bps to core PCE inflation; Apple's planned device price hikes could add another ~5bps.

bullets.title: TSMC to raise 2026 guidance at July 16 print: ~40% YoY revenue growth, $56B capex expected
bullets.body: Mizuho and Morgan Stanley Asia checks expect TSMC to raise both 2026 revenue guidance to ~40% YoY growth (vs prior ~35%) and capex to the high end of $52-56B range at July 16 earnings. N3 capacity is tracking to 170K wafers/month by 2026, N2 to 90K; CoWoS monthly capacity raised to 140K by 2026. TSMC is also negotiating 5-10% price increases for advanced nodes for 2027.

bullets.title: Korea announces $3.1T AI/semi capex through 2040; supply chain pricing hikes spreading
bullets.body: Samsung and SK Groups announced KRW 4,755T (~$3.1T) long-term capex through 2040 for semiconductors, AI data centers, and robotics. Equipment makers (ASML, AMAT, Lam, Tokyo Electron) have raised prices 5-15% from 2Q26; wafer fabs (Vanguard, UMC) are following with 5-15% hikes. Glass fiber cloth prices rising 30%+ effective July 1. JPM views 60-70% of Korean AI spend as flowing to front-end wafer/semis — bullish for SPEs.

bullets.title: AWS EC2 Capacity Block prices up ~20% July 1 — second hike this year; AI compute scarcity deepens
bullets.body: AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices ~20% effective July 1, the second increase this year after a ~15% January hike, confirming sustained pricing power for platform capacity. Long-term compute contract pricing is moving above Q1 neo-cloud benchmarks of $10-12M/MW due to xAI Colossus benchmarks and rising data center build costs. Labor shortages (electricians, skilled trades) and supply chain delays are becoming more common bottlenecks.

bullets.title: GOOGL PT raised to $415 at Morgan Stanley on 9GW 2028 compute capacity and Cloud hypergrowth
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises GOOGL PT to $415 (20% upside) modeling 9GW of incremental compute capacity in 2028 (7GW TPU, 2GW NVIDIA GPU), with Google Cloud projected to grow 106%/44% in 2027/2028 reaching $300B+. 2027/2028 capex modeled at $350B/$375B. 4GW of TPU merchant sales in 2028 at ~20% gross margin could generate ~$80B in revenue. Stock currently trades at 18X 2028 EPS vs 21X long-term average.

bullets.title: Solar stocks surge 11-15% on Trump administration draft ban on foreign inverters
bullets.body: The Trump administration is drafting a ban on imports of foreign inverters used in solar and battery projects, motivated by concerns China could use inverters to disrupt US power supplies. ENPH and SEDG rose 15%+ on the news; broader solar names up 3-11% in pre-market.

bullets.title: Chinese smartphone makers cutting 2026 shipment targets 30%; component shortages pressuring supply chain
bullets.body: Xiaomi cut its 2026 shipment target 30% to 95M units from 135M (down from 170M shipped in 2025); Oppo and Vivo have cut to below 90M units each. This is creating downstream memory demand pressure and contributing to market anxiety around unsustainable profit-sharing in the supply chain, with an Apple-MU pricing dispute crystallizing as a flashpoint.

bullets.title: European inflation decelerating faster than expected; Eurozone headline tracking toward 2.9% in June
bullets.body: French HICP fell 0.8pp to 2.0% YoY in June, well below JPM's 2.5% forecast. Italian HICP fell 0.1pp to 3.1%. German regional data points to a June print of 2.3-2.4% (down from 2.6% in May). Combined, France and Spain data point to Eurozone headline inflation declining from 3.2% to ~2.9% YoY in June — a meaningful beat that contributed to Q2's +14% equity return per UBS.

bullets.title: ECB hawkish bias intact; JPM expects final 25bp hike in September
bullets.body: ECB President Lagarde retained a clear hawkish bias at Sintra, moving back to 'measured' rate changes as the primary policy tool. JPM remains comfortable with a final 25bp hike in September, noting energy futures remain within ECB scenarios which assume three hikes. The economy is increasingly driven by supply shocks rather than demand shocks, supporting the case for measured action if growth remains resilient.

bullets.title: US consumer cash pile at record $22.9T — retail sales running 6.8% YoY; labor market resilient
bullets.body: JPM notes the US consumer cash pile hit a record $22.9T in 1Q26 (up from $14.8T pre-COVID), with all income brackets except the bottom 20th holding 8-29% more real cash than 2019. Retail sales growth has doubled post-COVID to ~6.8% YoY from ~3.4%. Q2 earnings season is tracking 22% earnings growth, 12.1% revenue growth, 14.1% margins — the S&P 500's best operating leverage since 2021.

bullets.title: JPM sees macro regime shift from slowdown to recovery; July NDX seasonality strongest month historically (+4.35%, 90% hit rate)
bullets.body: JPM's market intelligence team characterizes the macro regime as shifting from slowdown/stagflation to recovery/expansion, driven by lending pickup and normalized business sentiment. July is the NDX's best month over the last 10 years, averaging +4.35% with a 90% win rate. Fear/Greed was in Extreme Fear territory last Friday, providing upside room; ETF equity inflows totaled $33.9B with memory/semis as dominant flow themes.

bullets.title: US telcos (TMUS, VZ, T) down 4-6% on Starlink-Charter mobile threat; DT/TMUS merger fears add pressure
bullets.body: A Starlink-Charter consumer mobile partnership is being flagged as a structural threat to US telco incumbents, with TMUS, VZ, and AT&T all down 4-5%. Deutsche Telekom's CEO is reportedly exploring a holding structure to merge with T-Mobile US, though UBS argues the merger is unlikely given German government's 28.6% blocking stake and regulatory hurdles. Charter-satellite talks appear focused on CBRS spectrum complement, not a full wireless replacement.

bullets.title: Oil outlook: Morgan Stanley cuts 2027 Brent to $75/$70 as Hormuz normalizes; OPEC breakup risk rising
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lowered its 2027 Brent forecast to $75/bbl in 1H27 and $70/bbl in 2H27 as Strait of Hormuz reopening is tracking faster than expected. WTI is at $71.07 (+0.9%). Separately, OPEC faces breakup risk with Iraq considering an exit unless its quota is raised, which would pressure oil prices as Middle East producers prioritize market share over coordinated cuts.

bullets.title: Internet stocks face structural headwinds — JPM sees persistent overhangs preventing multiple names from working
bullets.body: JPM's internet team characterizes investor sentiment at 4-year lows, with company-specific overhangs on META (negative-ROIC superintelligence lab), AMZN (elevated capex $300-400B vs Street $245B, consumer softness), GOOGL (capex clarity needed), NFLX (anemic US engagement), SPOT (AI tier delayed to 2027), DASH (US order growth deceleration), and BKNG (agentic AI bear case exposure). APP remains the standout, contingent on eComm inflection.

bullets.title: SMCI Taiwan offices raided in chip smuggling probe; DRAM price-fixing class action filed
bullets.body: Taiwanese authorities raided Super Micro Computer's Taiwan offices as part of an expanded probe into alleged Nvidia chip smuggling into China. Separately, a class-action lawsuit was filed against three major DRAM makers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) for alleged price-fixing, though prevailing analysis attributes price increases to AI demand and HBM surge rather than collusion.
